title: The camera
content: A camera is an optical instrument that forms and records an image of an object.

title: Convex lens
content: A convex lens focuses the light from the object to form a real inverted image on the film or electronic sensor.

title: Diaphragm
content: A diaphragm is placed behind the convex lens to control the amount of light energy falling on the film.

title: Aperture
content: The aperture is a circular opening through which the light passes. It can be made wide or narrow by adjusting the diaphragm. The size of the diameter of the aperture is expressed in term of f- numbers. The f- number of a camera is the ratio of the focal length of the lens to the diameter of aperture.

title: Shutter
content: A shutter controls the time during which light enters the camera through the lens.

title: Focusing Ring
content: A camera consists of a focusing ring by which the distance between the lens and the film can be adjusted to obtain a sharp image on the film.

title: Film
content: The film at the back of the camera is actually a screen which receives the image. In a digital camera, the film is replaced by an electronic sensor. It is made up of millions of tiny pixels which response to light.

title: Human eye
content: Human eye consists of sense organs which are capable of receiving visual images and sending the information to the brain.

title: Farsightedness (Hyperopia)
content: Farsightedness is a defect of vision in which distant objects are seen clearly, but objects nearby are blurry.

title: Nearsightedness (Myopia)
content: Nearsightedness is a defect of vision in which near objects are seen clearly, but objects far away are blurry.

title: Least distance of distinct vision
content: People with normal vision can be seen an object in greatest detail when it is placed at a certain distance from the eye. This distance, which is known as the least distance of distinct vision is about 25 cm.

title: Maximum distance of distinct vision
content: People with normal vision can see clearly objects which are at infinity. Thus, for normal vision for the maximum distance of distinct vision is infinity.

title: Compound microscope
content: A microscope is an optical instrument which uses lenses to make enlarged images of objects that are too small for the unaided eye to see.

title: Electron microscope
content: Electron microscope is a microscope with high magnification and resolution, employing electron beams in place of light and using electron lenses.

title: Telescope
content: An optical instrument used for viewing distant objects is called a telescope.

title: Astronomical telescope
content: The refracting astronomical telescope consists of an objective of long focal length and an eyepiece of short focal length.

title: Total reflecting prisms
content: Total reflecting prisms (90°, 45°, 45° prisms) are used in binoculars to reduce the length of the terrestrial telescope.

title: Binocular
content: A binocular is an optical instrument which consists of a pair of telescopes one for each eye, and those telescope employ the total reflecting prism.

title: Laser
content: A laser, acronym for Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation, is a source of a narrow beam of intense, monochromatic, coherent light in the visible, infrared or ultraviolet part of the electromagnetic radiation.

title: Spectrometer
content: A spectrometer is a scientific instrument used to separate and measure spectral components of a physical phenomenon.

title: Photometry
content: Photometry is the science of measuring visible light in units that are weighted to the sensitive of human eye. The human eye responds only to light having wavelengths between about 400 nm and 700 nm.

title: Luminance
content: Luminance L_v is the luminous intensity per unit area of light travelling in a given direction.

title: Inverse square law of illuminance
content: The luminance E_v at any point on the surface is inversely proportional to the square of the distance r between the source and the surface. This is known as inverse square law of illuminance.
